explanation: The first sentence describes a big challenge (building an accurate model of Earth's shape), and the second names who finally made those calculations possible. "Ultimately" signals that end result. "In addition" and "Secondly" treat the sentence as just another item in a list, and "In other words" wrongly suggests a restatement.

The goal is to explain where the name comes from. A says the shower is named for Perseus because its radiant sits in that constellation, which links the name to its source. D mentions Perseus but never says the shower is named after it, and B and C don't mention Perseus at all.
Only A gives a title, Babel-17, and says it won a Nebula Award. B and D refer to Delany's novel without naming it, and C doesn't mention a specific novel.

The text lists two jobs guard cells do: regulating carbon dioxide intake and regulating water loss. "Additionally" adds the second job to the first. "Instead" would wrongly mean the second job replaces the first, and "In conclusion" doesn't fit a new point.

A contrast needs both numbers set against each other. D uses "Whereas" to compare the metal fibers' 0.02 emissivity with the silicon carbide fibers' 0.74. C says the rates were different but gives no values, so it doesn't actually show the contrast.

D makes a general claim (a comet's orbit can change over time) and backs it up with the specific case of 81P/Wild. C gives only the example with no generalization, and A makes a general statement without supporting evidence.

The first sentence claims that a more diverse generation of conductors is emerging, and de la Parra and Gonzalez-Granados are examples of that trend. "For instance" introduces examples. "In addition" would treat them as a separate point rather than as support for the claim.

The blank introduces where Anning made her discoveries, and the next sentence confirms her work put the Jurassic Coast on the map. "There" points back to Lyme Regis on the Jurassic Coast. "For example" fails because her discoveries aren't an example of where she lived.

The first sentence says broadly that auroras result from the Sun's activity, and the next sentences give the precise mechanism. "Specifically" moves from the general idea to the details. "Hence" would wrongly make the particles a consequence of the auroras.

To show why Amos's enlistment date matters historically, C ties it to the Civil War (1861–1865) and notes he was one of the few Filipino sailors to serve in it. A compares his date to Ignases's but never says why 1863 matters, and D focuses on Ignases.
Only A states the publication year, 1025 CE. The other choices describe the author or the book's later use without giving the year.

An audience unfamiliar with the Haudenosaunee Confederacy needs the theory stated and the Great Law of Peace explained. C does both: it defines the Great Law as an agreement binding six Native nations and says it influenced the US Constitution. B uses the names without explaining them, and A never says what the law influenced.

The goal is about green signs specifically. B contrasts where green directional signs are used: on both highways and major roads in the US, but only on major roads in the UK. A focuses on blue signs, and C stresses a similarity, not a contrast.

B emphasizes what McKay achieved before Harlem: two acclaimed poetry collections published in 1912 while he lived in Jamaica. A mixes those works with later Harlem works, and D lists only works written after he moved.

The first sentence explains that scientists believed in phlogiston, and the second shows a result of that belief: Priestley named oxygen "dephlogisticated air." "For this reason" signals that cause and effect. "Nevertheless" would wrongly suggest Priestley's naming went against the phlogiston theory, when it actually followed from it.
A similarity needs something the two sites share. D notes that both are examples of ancient rock art in Somaliland. B describes a difference, and A and C each mention only one site.

The second sentence backs up and intensifies the claim that the installation is whimsical yet perplexing, describing visitors as dazzled and confused. "Indeed" signals that kind of confirmation. "Nevertheless" would imply a contrast that isn't there.
The 2018 exhibition was Pacha, Llaqta, Wasichay, and B names it and says it featured seven emerging Latino artists. A describes the 2020 exhibition instead, and C and D don't identify the 2018 show.

The researchers want scientists to avoid the word "life," and the next sentence gives the replacement they suggest, "lyfe." "Instead" signals that substitution. "Regardless" would ignore the link between the two sentences.

Because recent research shows the episode was less frenzied and disastrous than believed, it follows that the popular myth deserves skepticism. "Therefore" signals this conclusion. "Nevertheless" would imply the skepticism goes against the research, when the research is the reason for it.

Most of the observed females laid eggs in many other ducks' nests, but 7F64B visited only a few sites and then raised her own eggs, a different strategy. "Alternatively" signals that different option. "For example" and "in particular" would wrongly present her as a case of the parasitic behavior, and "similarly" claims a likeness that doesn't exist.

Ostrom showed that people can sustainably manage shared resources themselves, and because of that, her work rejects the idea that shared resources will inevitably be overused. "As such" draws this consequence. "By contrast" and "That said" suggest a conflict, but the second sentence follows directly from the first.

The audience already knows Kang and Fung, so the sentence should just say where Fung is in the photo. D does this: she's seated on the floor with her paintings behind her. A and B spend space introducing Kang, and C mentions only the paintings, not Fung's position.
B names a specific fruit, pineapple, that contains vitamin C. A and C talk about fruits or food in general without giving an example, and D doesn't mention fruit at all.

Each Ice Age erases the evidence of the one before it, so geologists struggled to confirm that Ice Ages repeat. "Hence" signals that result. "Nevertheless" would suggest a contrast, but the delay follows naturally from the lost evidence.

To contrast the samples, the sentence must point to a difference between them. D does this by noting that the SEBS sample (4 mm) was thicker than the TPU sample (3 mm). A states a similarity (both heated up), and B and C don't compare the samples.

The finding was that the brain can switch between two ways of processing smells: capturing information at a moment and tracking changes over time. D summarizes exactly that. A and C focus on the study's method, and B gives only one of the two methods.

B presents both the study (an analysis of the map's ink in 2021) and its findings (a titanium compound used only since the 1920s, so the map is from the twentieth century). A, C, and D describe the study but leave out its conclusion.

The question is why historians credit Abele. A gives the reason: the campus buildings use the styles Abele had studied in Europe. B and D state the belief without the reasoning, and C never connects the styles to Abele's training.
"After" makes the order clear: the UK march came first, then the US march. C reverses the order, and B and D don't compare the timing of both marches.

The text sets two views of space side by side: quantitative analysts measured it with GIS technology, while Massey defined it through social and political forces. "By contrast" signals that difference, which the word "instead" in the sentence also hints at. "Likewise" and "for example" would wrongly treat Massey as agreeing with the GIS approach.

fix.passage: In the late twentieth century, scholars directed much discussion toward issues of spatiality. Adherents to quantitative analytical approaches delineated space with the use of GIS spatial technologies; ______ cultural geographer Doreen Massey defined space as the product of “an ever-shifting social geometry of power and signification,” focusing instead on socio-political forces.

explanation: D explains what harvestmen are: arachnids, also called daddy longlegs, but not spiders. A and C wrongly call them spiders, and B mentions daddy longlegs without explaining what they are.

Bots learned to read distorted text, and in reaction a new version of reCAPTCHA that tracks cursor movement was released. "In response" signals that reaction. "For example" fails because the new version isn't an example of bots getting better.

The writer admits a point that seems to weaken the claim (many dances share order and repetition) before explaining what still makes the Madison special. "Of course" introduces that kind of concession. "However" doesn't fit, because the admission doesn't contradict the description of the Madison; the "but" later in the sentence provides the contrast.

D makes a generalization (different definitions lead to very different island counts) and supports it with Sweden's 221,000 versus 24 islands. B is close but stays vague and gives no supporting numbers, and A and C don't generalize about the definitions.

Practical effects look real but can be too expensive, and that cost is why filmmakers mix them with CGI. "For this reason" signals that cause and effect. "Similarly" and "Furthermore" miss the cause-and-effect link.
Since the quad axel is such an extreme feat, it makes sense that the audience was awestruck. "Fittingly" signals that the reaction matched the achievement. "However" would wrongly suggest a contrast.

The text says the directors love cats, and the next sentence strengthens that claim with striking proof: they made a whole game about a cat. "In fact" signals that kind of emphasis. "Nevertheless" and "On the other hand" imply a contrast that isn't there.
Only A gives Tecozautla's size, roughly 535 km². The other choices discuss services or the number of municipalities without saying how big Tecozautla is.

The text compares two kinds of monopsony: a single buyer forcing lower prices and employers forcing lower wages work the same way. "Similarly" signals this parallel. "Instead" would wrongly suggest the second replaces the first.
C introduces the 1983 collection by naming it (Precario/Precarious), its publisher, and its author. A only mentions it in passing, and B and D don't name it.

The second clause backs up the claim that Iceland's volcanoes are extreme outliers by showing how much shallower most volcanoes' magma sources are. "Indeed" introduces this supporting point. "Consequently" fails because the shallow magma of other volcanoes isn't caused by Iceland's depths.
D gives the full order: Commerce Department, then the CAA in 1938, then the FAA in 1958. A gets the order wrong, B says the times differed without giving the order, and C mentions only the FAA.

Researchers widened the grooves in the wood, and because of that the grooves became wide enough to fit conductors. "As a result" signals this effect. "For example" and "In contrast" don't match the cause-and-effect relationship.

A narrative about creating the robots should start at the beginning: the ants that inspired Ozkan-Aydin to design them. C does that. A describes how the finished robots work, B starts at the end of the process, and D doesn't mention her.
Most deer species have antlers only on males, but reindeer break that pattern. "However" signals the contrast. "Similarly" would wrongly say reindeer follow the same pattern.

D states a clear difference: C-type asteroids are mostly carbon, while S-type asteroids are mostly silicate minerals. A and B mention both types without contrasting them, and C gives only one percentage.

The text follows two characters at the same time: Ifemelu goes to the US while Obinze goes to London. "Meanwhile" signals events happening in parallel. "Nevertheless" implies a contrast that isn't there, and "Secondly" doesn't fit a story.

Majoritarian systems tend to produce two parties, while proportional systems tend to produce many parties, which is the opposite outcome. "Conversely" signals that contrast. "For instance" and "In other words" wrongly treat the second sentence as an example or restatement of the first.
Singletary often collaborates with other artists, and his work with Naranjo is one case of that. "For example" introduces the illustration. "However" suggests a contrast that isn't there.

Scientists need unchanging measurement standards, and that need is why the SI was developed. "For this reason" signals that cause and effect. "In contrast" and "Regardless" miss the link between the two sentences.
B states directly that the pineapple has fifty chromosomes. C says only that it has more than the melon, A never gives a number, and D is about the melon.

D makes a general claim (the Alta conflict had a lasting impact) and supports it with specifics: international attention and legal protections for Sámi rights. B makes the claim with no support, A only describes the protests, and C gives the specifics without a general claim.

D contrasts the meters correctly: Meghadūta uses long and short syllables (quantitative), while Widsith uses repeated sounds (alliterative). A contrasts the languages, not the meters, C wrongly gives Widsith a pattern of long and short syllables, and B doesn't mention the poems.
Raw acorns are very bitter, so the Tongva had to process them before eating them. "Therefore" signals that result. "However" would wrongly suggest a contrast.

C presents both findings accurately: the marigold FTWs removed phosphorus and also produced market-quality blooms. B wrongly applies the 52% to blooms instead of phosphorus, and D garbles the numbers (52% more phosphorus than the control, not 52% of it; 65 blooms per square meter, not 65 total).

choices.A: The authors concluded that marigolds grown on FTWs were “commercially viable,” having produced 65 blooms per square meter of market-quality blooms in a 2023 study.

explanation: Because the chemical strengthens the bonds between water molecules, the molecules keep their structure under extreme pressure. "As a result" signals this effect. "Nevertheless" and "However" imply a contrast that isn't there.

Radio listeners thought Kennedy lost, yet the debate was ultimately considered his victory. "Nevertheless" signals this contrast with the expectation set up in the first sentence. "Therefore" wrongly suggests the poll led to his being seen as the winner.

The text lists Franklin's anti-counterfeiting steps: special threads and muscovite in the paper, plus detailed sage-leaf imprints. "Moreover" adds another step to the list. "Specifically" and "For example" fail because the sage-leaf stamp isn't a detail of the paper-weaving step that came before.

B both explains Aeolian landforms (landforms created by the wind) and gives an example, the mushroom rock, with how the wind shapes it. A explains without a concrete example, C wrongly treats mushroom rocks as separate from Aeolian landforms, and D never defines Aeolian landforms.
Only C gives the location: near the University of Wisconsin–Madison. A gives the name and year but not where it was housed.

For readers who don't know Angkor Wat, C briefly identifies it as a Cambodian temple and presents Tan's research: a new imaging technique that revealed hundreds of hidden images. A and B never explain what Angkor Wat is, and D leaves out Tan and his research.
C defines a quenched galaxy as one that no longer forms stars, which is the explanation the student needs. A, B, and D mention quenching but never say what a quenched galaxy actually is.

The second sentence backs up the claim that the archive's audio collection is impressive with a striking detail: more than 5,000 recordings going back to 1943. "In fact" introduces that support. "Instead" and "Regardless" imply a contrast or dismissal that doesn't fit.
The aim of the study was to find out whether woodland expansion is related to climate change, and A states that goal. B and C give the results, and D describes the method.

The text describes the steps of a process in order ("First," "Next"), and slipping the paper through the liquid is the last step. "Finally" marks that last step. "Therefore" wrongly suggests cause and effect.

The first sentence explains that drawing in oxygen produces the glow, and the second describes the opposite situation: when the oxygen stops, so does the glow. "By contrast" signals that opposite case. "For instance" and "Specifically" fail because the second sentence isn't an example or detail of the first.

The second sentence supports the claim that the space felt both familiar (like a movie theater) and distant (inside a coal mine). "Indeed" introduces that confirming detail. "Nevertheless" and "Instead" suggest a contrast that isn't there.

The fossil's significance is that it shows an early stage in the evolution of pinnipeds from land animals, and C states this while describing its mix of four legs and a seal's skull. A and D describe the fossil without explaining why it matters, and B is vague about what the fossil resembles.

The poem seems to offer little to analyze, yet Berlant finds plenty to say about it. "Nonetheless" signals that contrast. "Likewise" and "That is" would wrongly suggest Berlant agrees the poem is barren.

The geyser's cycle seems hostile to life, but it is actually home to many bacteria. "Still" signals this contrast with what you might expect. "Thus" wrongly suggests the geyser's harshness causes the biodiversity.

The text says the research was very influential, and the next sentence gives a concrete case of that influence: it laid the groundwork for the 1987 treaty. "Specifically" introduces that detail. "However" implies a contrast, and "Earlier" gets the timing wrong, since the treaty came after the research.

The first sentence says broadly that the study looked at spending and performance, and the second gives the specifics: overhead costs compared with event attendance for 22,328 nonprofits. "Specifically" introduces those details. "In addition" would wrongly treat this as a second study.

Above the Kármán line, lift no longer keeps an aircraft up, so it stays aloft by speed rather than lift. "Instead" signals this replacement of one mechanism with another. "For instance" and "Granted" don't capture that substitution.

A contrasts the two maps' purposes with "while": the opening map introduces the world, and the closing map helps readers retrace the story. C says each map has a purpose without saying what, and B and D don't mention purposes.
Still was famous in his own time, yet he is discussed much less today. "However" signals that contrast. "Similarly" and "For example" don't fit the change from fame to neglect.

The text describes a shift toward collaboration over time, shown by a rise in multi-author publications. "Increasingly" captures that growing trend. "For this reason" doesn't work, because the shift isn't a cause of mathematicians collaborating; it is the collaborating.
After hours or even days of simmering, the cloth is finally taken out. "Eventually" signals the step that comes after that long wait. "Nevertheless" and "Likewise" don't fit a sequence of steps.

By combining Native and non-Native symbols in one object, Gibson's piece also blurs the line between art and craft. "In so doing" ties that second effect to the same act of combining. "Conversely" implies a contrast, and "For instance" and "In particular" fail because blurring art and craft isn't an example of mixing cultural symbols.

fix.passage: Jeffrey Gibson’s sculptural object KNOW YOUR MAGIC, BABY, an Everlast-brand exercise bag embroidered with multicolored beads and a fringe associated with the dances of the Ojibwe people, stitches together—literally and figuratively—recognizable symbols from both Native and non-Native cultures. ______ Gibson’s piece also blurs the distinction between contemporary art and traditional crafts.

explanation: The goal is to compare disadvantages of both systems. C names the docked programs' drawback (they require more resources) and alludes to the dockless programs' drawback (organizational problems). A mentions only the dockless downside, B gets flexibility backwards, and D doesn't discuss disadvantages.
